answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy creates an oasis of trust by anchoring identity to a cryptographic stake-burning jetty that extends into economic friction. Each minted identity burns non-refundable jade tokens where aggregate cost scales superlinearly: registering k identities costs O(k^2) tokens. This quadratic friction ensures attacker expenditure grows exponentially relative to network yield, rendering identity flooding economically ruinous.
